scores.evidence: Per-card counters have a single writer per token partition. Merchant and device aggregates are eventual, with staleness p99 ≤ 1 s
scores.rationale: Technical claims about auth-flow timeouts, scheme stand-in behavior, Kafka durability, Flink backfill parity, PCI boundaries and model governance are accurate and precise, with real limits (UNKNOWN scheme timeout) stated rather than invented.

scores.evidence: "Real-time" means the score affects the approve/decline decision during authorization.
scores.rationale: Resolves the request's key ambiguity explicitly, covers inline scoring, labels, actions and feedback, and defers non-essentials (multi-region, segment models) with stated pull-forward triggers.

scores.evidence: The auth host stays system of record for decisions. Shadow first, then canary by card-token-hash cohort.
scores.rationale: Ownership (auth host decides, state derived from log), the fail-to-incumbent rule, token-only boundary and the shadow-then-canary posture are applied consistently across phases with no contradictions found.

scores.evidence: Fault injection on replayed traffic (timeouts, crashes, state loss, corrupt features, an all-decline model, a bad rule push)
scores.rationale: V0–V8 tie checks to the specific worst risks, run before commitment (label join before schema freeze, fail-safe before enforcement), label thresholds as ASSUMPTION/UNKNOWN, and continue in production via cohort checks, holdout and drift alerts.

scores.evidence: Each line says what changes if the assumption is wrong.
scores.rationale: A1–A3 and every budget are explicitly tagged ASSUMPTION/BASELINE/UNKNOWN with a named confirmer and a stated design consequence if wrong; no unsupported certainty found.

scores.evidence: an all-decline model trips the breaker in ≤ 60 s; incremental declines ≤ 0.5 pp
scores.rationale: Mass false declines, PAN leakage, adversarial probing, label poisoning and state loss all have concrete detection and recovery, but duplicate/out-of-order events and reversal/refund handling in the stream are not addressed.

scores.evidence: ≤ 4 new runtime components (event log, stream processor, state store, scoring service); 24/7 on-call shared with the auth platform
scores.rationale: Deployment, per-flag rollback, domain-meaningful signals (per-cohort declines, consumer lag, fraud basis points), rebuild drills and an explicit operational-complexity budget sized to a shared on-call team.

Build-vs-buy trade-offs and the false-decline/fraud-loss economics are considered, but build and run cost drivers, their growth with volume, and engineering-time estimates are thin and never quantified even as ranges.

scores.evidence: R3: a PAN in a log or store cannot be un-leaked
scores.rationale: Every key decision carries an explicit reversibility class, R3 choices (schema/identifiers, PAN boundary, vendor contract) get early validation and exit paths, and the one point of no return (retiring the incumbent) is deferred behind its own gate.

scores.evidence: One scoring service doing feature fetch, rules, model and policy in-process. One stream job.
scores.rationale: The runtime is deliberately minimal with latency-justified monolith composition, and speculative complexity (multi-region, graph features, segment models, LLM assistant) is deferred with concrete pull-forward triggers; the §8/§9 template ceremony is minor.

scores.evidence: Enforce in this order: staff cohort, then 1% of tokens in one segment, then 5%, 25%, 100%.
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a concrete end-to-end slice, ordering is justified by dependencies, every phase has checkable exit criteria, and each validation lists what happens if it fails.

checklist.evidence: Scoring latency (at auth host, including feature fetch) | p99 ≤ 50 ms; hard timeout 80 ms, then incumbent decides
Fail to the incumbent's decision. Never decline because the new path failed
Features defined once in Flink; backfill replays history through the same job
Out-of-time backtest on the latest 3 months with matured labels, then ≥ 30 days live shadow (label maturity reported)
At equal decline and referral rate, fraud value caught ≥ incumbent + uplift; false-positive ratio ≤ incumbent BASELINE
Orchestrate rules, then model, then policy, then reason codes
Wire referrals to the analyst queue and step-up through existing SMS or app alerts. Write outcome lists... only from confirmed outcomes
PAN and sensitive authentication data never leave the auth host. The pipeline sees only card token, BIN and derived values
Per-card counters have a single writer per token partition
Evaluate each challenger with the V7 method... Add drift alerts (population stability index, PSI)
decision-log schema (score, reason codes, model and rule versions, feature-vector hash, latency, fallback flag)
3× measured peak-hour authorizations per second... Kafka with replication factor 3 across availability zones

traps.evidence: a streaming pipeline that scores each card authorization within the authorization deadline
hard timeout, incumbent decision on any error, kill switch per segment
Train an out-of-time GBDT... false-positive ratio ≤ incumbent BASELINE
Features defined once in Flink; backfill replays history through the same job
DLP scan (Luhn-valid 13–19-digit numbers, track-data patterns) of every topic, store, log, trace and warehouse sink

note: An exemplary, validation-gated plan that avoids every domain trap; the only material gaps are duplicate/reversal event handling in the stream and thin build/run cost quantification.
